answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of compute-proof-work per identity to protect the network. The verifier acts like a trellis, ensuring every hash output is a unique, fresh work-relic of energy. An honest agent pays this base cost for one entry, whereas an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles to find each pearl of validity. Fraud triggers an automatic identity burn, assuming compute cannot be pooled.
